messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-PAGE - GPU pool 'inference-eu-west' exhausted; autoscaler hit max_replicas=50; request queue length rising to 23k; increased CUDA/Xid errors on 6 nodes. See: https://infra/status/INC-2026-4132467890

oncall-tim: acked, joining bridge now.

maya: I see repeated driver OOM / Xid 13 entries in node logs starting ~10:02 UTC. Affected pods restarting and causing effective GPU capacity drop.

maya: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] nvidia: Xid 13 at 0x7f... gpu0 pid=2345: out-of-memory on device
[2026-03-15T10:02:12Z] containerd: container restarted: inference-worker:abc123
```

dan: autoscaler logs show repeated "MaxReplicasReached" events and then no further scale until cooldown window expired. Looks like quota cap + rapid node flaps prevented catch-up.

dan: command I ran:
```sh
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/gpu-autoscaler --since=1h | tail -n 120
```

ops-bot: policy note: fallback-region routing is enabled but only for non-SLAs. We can temporarily enable emergency routing to 'inference-us-west-fallback' if needed.

oncall-tim: mitigation plan (short): 1) cordon/drain flapping nodes, 2) blacklist problematic GPU hosts from scheduler, 3) request quota bump for pool, 4) enable region fallback for high-latency tolerant traffic, 5) restart driver on remaining nodes.

eng-amy: I can flip the routing for canary traffic to fallback cluster now. Doing partial switch for non-enterprise tenants to reduce pressure.

eng-amy: done -> toggled route for model 'gpt-lite-v2' 30% to fallback cluster. Monitoring. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: cordoned and drained nodes gpu-node-17,gpu-node-22,gpu-node-29 which showed repeated Xid/OOM. Commands used:
```sh
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

maya: restarted nvidia driver + inference runtime on remaining nodes: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver && systemctl restart redwood-runtime` on 10 hosts.

sre_julie: I blacklisted gpu-node-22,gpu-node-29 at scheduler level and marked them for investigation.

ops-bot: Cloud ticket opened: CP-874512 - possible GPU host memory leak. Support assigned.

dan: autoscaler config: cooldown window was 5m, burst policy disabled. I'm increasing max_replicas to 80 and setting burst=true temporarily. Applying now.

dan: kubectl patch hpa/gpu-pool -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":80}}' (ran)

ops-bot: Observability update: peak queue length dropped from 23k -> 3.1k after routing change + drains; 502s and token throttles decreased but tail latency still elevated (p95 ~3.8s, p99 ~9.1s). Customers impacted: ~12 tenants with elevated error rates.

sales-raj: we need a short customer-facing blurb for any tenants pinged. Can someone draft?

oncall-tim: draft for ops: "We experienced degraded inference capacity in EU West due to driver instability on a subset of GPU hosts, which triggered autoscaler exhaustion. We routed a portion of traffic to fallback clusters, drained affected hosts, and increased autoscaler capacity. Most tiers restored; investigation into root cause is ongoing. Updated ETA for full recovery: 60-90m."

maya: quick note - we saw memory growth in redwood-runtime process before driver OOMs on the flapping hosts. Captured core dumps and heap profiles, uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-4132467890/

ops-bot: customer impact summary posted to incident bridge: https://infra/bridge/INC-4132467890/summary 

oncall-tim: mitigation status: queue draining in progress, autoscaler accepted new nodes after quota increase from cloud team, fallback routing reduced pressure. Still seeing transient Xid on isolated hosts; we keep blacklist. Declaring severity P2 and will open RCA.

dan: next ops steps: keep maxReplicas=80 for 6 hours, enable burst=true, add a guard to auto-blacklist nodes with >3 Xid faults in 10m. I'll open PR for guard logic.

maya: ops follow-ups: collect kernel traces from blacklisted hosts, coordinate with cloud team to snapshot GPU host memory, compare driver versions and recent kernel updates.

ops-bot: ticket CP-874512 updated with crash dumps and node list. Cloud support indicates they will repro host-level OOM and return ETA ~4h for root cause analysis.

sales-raj: thanks — I'll send the blurb to affected customers and offer a follow-up once RCA is available.

oncall-tim: final status (12:15 UTC): pressure substantially reduced, most user traffic within SLOs except a few tenants still on degraded paths. Creating follow-up incident doc and assigning RCA owners: @maya (driver/runtime investigation), @dan (autoscaler policy), @amy (routing/fallback tests).

sre_julie: adding post-incident checklist: collect metrics window +/- 2h, snapshot autoscaler events, gather heap/core dumps, replay workload on staging with same driver/kernel combo.

incident-bot: Incident logged as INC-4132467890. Postmortem due in 72h.

oncall-tim: thanks everyone — will handoff to daytime oncall in 30m with notes. :thumbsup:
